sections.title: What you know
sections.content: You know how to look back at a mistake with *Deberías haber llamado* from B2 Unit 10, and the verbs *quejarse* from B2 Unit 5 and *criticar* from B2 Unit 14. When you report such a reproach, the verb *reprochar* (or *echar en cara*) is the one that says what was said: not just that someone spoke, but that they blamed someone. It takes *que* and the subjunctive; for something that was not done in the past, use the pluperfect subjunctive from B2 Unit 16.

sections.title: Reproach and blame
rows: reprochar / echar en cara + que + subjunctive
Me reprochó que no hubiera llamado.
reprochar + haber + participle (the person blamed acted)
acusar a alguien de + haber + participle
Me acusó de haber llegado tarde.

sections.title: Which verb?
sections.content: *Reprochar* and *echar en cara* report a complaint about something that was not done as it should have been. «Deberías haber llamado» and «No llamaste» are both reported as *Me reprochó que no hubiera llamado*. *Culpar* and *acusar* name the fault the person is held responsible for, with *de* and a noun or *haber* + participle. Do not use *que* after them.

items.spanish: Ana me reprochó que no hubiera llamado antes.
items.english: Ana reproached me for not having called earlier.

items.spanish: Me echó en cara que no la hubiera ayudado.
items.english: She threw it in my face that I had not helped her.

items.spanish: Me acusó de haber olvidado la llave.
items.english: He accused me of having forgotten the key.

items.spanish: Los vecinos culparon al alcalde del problema.
items.english: The neighbours blamed the mayor for the problem.

sections.content: When the person blamed is the one who acted, the infinitive is usually smoother: *Me reprochó no haber llamado*. When the blame falls on a third person, keep *que*: *Le reprochó que su hermano no hubiera llamado*.
